steps.content: The journey isn't peaceful. You pass collapsed houses and ruins while Oak Casket remains unusually silent. The only thing that alleviates your unease is the faint, unique fragrance on her.

You keep wondering what the little girl was reciting, and what the light represents. The recitation sounded like a prayer from someone from the monastery, but Oak Casket's unusual reaction tells you that this is no simple prayer.
Thinking this, you look at Oak Casket walking ahead of you.
She seems to never want to stop for the scenery around her, yet she's the messenger who always stops and turns back to listen to those who can't go on.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What's the matter?
Noticing that you haven't kept up, Oak Casket turns around and asks simply.
Nothing... I'm just a little surprised by the lack of signs of habitation here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This place...
Oak Casket looks at the flat land around her with a calm expression that doesn't give away any emotions.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's because this place is a mass grave.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Initially, stray dogs would forage around here in packs. No one wanted to be near here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Later, to curb Mania, this place was hastily buried and covered up. But even though the smell was gone, most people still avoided this area. Only until recently... After the war ended, people began to remember this place after Romanesque's been destroyed.
Only then do you see some recent mounds on the land originally covered with weeds. Not far away, someone is erecting a plank of wood in front of a mound as a makeshift gravestone.
As the man plants the plank into the earth, he keeps muttering something, his voice drifting in the air along with the flickering phosphorescence.
You shall endure hardships... Meet the golden falcon... Traveler will guide you to the light...
You finally understand why those words in the vision sounded so familiar.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Perhaps you have.
You were reciting it when I entered the interrogation room.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world... You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Now you want to ask: Where did you learn about this poem?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Well... This is an elegy that reminds the dead to let go of all suffering and prays that they can travel to the beautiful and peaceful land of eternity.
Have you heard someone recite it?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: More precisely, someone recited it for me.
But you just said this is an elegy for the dead...
Before entering the interrogation room, you looked over the investigation report on Oak Casket.

She was born during Syndicate's most chaotic period. Orphaned since a young age, she was adopted by a priest from the monastery. When she was about thirteen, the monastery was destroyed in a gang fight, and the priest died that year.
Ever since then, the teenage girl has disappeared from the official records.
How many deaths and departures must she have witnessed over all these years to become what she is now?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You're looking very earnest now. Are you that eager to delve into my past?
As the Chief of the Bureau, and as your friend, I want to know.
Oak Casket gives a slight smile, but it doesn't melt the frosty chill on her face.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Very well... I'm looking forward to your response to this story, little one.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It took place when this mass grave hadn't been covered up yet.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: At that time, I was one of the hundreds of corpses in the pit. But I was not dead. I was thrown in alive.
The smell of blood stung her nose. The little girl struggled to open her eyes.
So stinky. So disgusting. I want to get out of this place.
But she couldn't move. Rigid bodies were lying on top of her limbs, belly, and shoulders. The body she was leaning against was also slowly turning cold.
She finally realized what was happening. She looked up and saw the gray sky several meters above.
The gravely injured girl was lying at the bottom of the pit helplessly.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: I'm still alive...
Weak and with her throat parched, she could only make a faint noise.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Please... Help me...
Soon after, footsteps came from above the pit.
Two figures stood at the edge of the pit and noticed the little girl at the bottom with her eyes open.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Father... Doctor...

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: Help me... Help me, please...
They seemed to be muttering something. A moment later, another body was thrown down.

steps.speaker: Old Priest & Doctor
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light...
Hearing the words, she watched more and more bodies being thrown into the pit. Dirt was being shoveled onto her head, covering her view.

steps.speaker: Little Girl
steps.content: You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What's the point? He told me to seek the light when he cast me into the dark.
Oak Casket recalls placidly, her voice gradually merging with the little girl's in the vision. A rough guess arises in your mind.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The living believe their prayers can cleanse the souls of the dead, helping them find relief. They cover up their sins with such grandiose rhetoric, as if they can earn forgiveness from the dead just like that.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This poem won't bring light. It's just an excuse for the living to absolve themselves and alleviate their guilt.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Once they finish reciting the poem, the death of the deceased has nothing to do with the living anymore.
Oak Casket looks at you composedly.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Alright, little one, you got your story...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: In return, can you give me a guiding answer?
You can't find the strength or words to argue with her anymore. After all, what words carry enough weight to comfort who was once discarded by the living?
Oak Casket shrugs. Without taking one last glimpse at this land, she walks straight ahead.
You remain silent all the way, following Oak Casket to an old residential building.
The building is on the verge of collapse, the exterior wrapped in a mess of electrical cables. You climb the narrow staircase to the first floor and knock on the door, but no one answers.
Are you sure this is the place?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I can't be mistaken.

Oak Casket produces a thin slice of metal out of nowhere and slides it through the door gap effortlessly, like performing surgery. When the door opens, the entire frame shakes like it may collapse at any moment.

As soon as the door opens, a stench hits you. Several rats squeal and scurry past you. The living room is filled with all sorts of garbage, from which a bunch of flies take off and try to land on you.

You walk through a dark corridor. The light should be on, as you can hear the hum of electricity in the light bulb, but it's not lit. Perhaps it's stayed on for too long. The faucet is stuck with rust, and occasionally you can hear water dripping.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Hmm, he's still alive.
What?
Oak Casket draws the curtains of the room open. With the faint morning light filtering in through the window, you see a person lying on the bed.

Half of the body is shriveled up under a faded old quilt, revealing only a dried and wrinkled face and sparse white hair. If it weren't for his breathing, you'd almost mistake it for a dried-up skeleton.
Is this the doctor?
Oak Casket doesn't speak and simply nods. Her expression remains indifferent. You can't tell what she thinks of this situation.
You lean in toward the doctor, trying to wake him up.
Excuse me, Sir.
The doctor doesn't move. You smell the stench of bedsores. He must have been paralyzed for quite some time, and with no one taking care of him, his bed reeks of excrement.
Is this... nutritional fluid?
You see a half-used bottle of liquid lying on the bedside table, guessing it might be what's keeping him alive.
He's neither dead nor alive, cut off from all possibilities of communication.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What a shame. He's worthless in his state.
...What?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Isn't he? In his current state, he can't even speak clearly.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But if he died, we could at least learn something from him through my ability.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The dead are honest while the living are furtive. The dead are tranquil while the living are restless. The dead are eternally peaceful and loyal; as the root of all evil, the living create nothing but chaos.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You see, I like the dead a little more than the living.
Oak Casket's eyes somewhat soften as she says this.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Given his condition, only death can grant him relief.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What's the point of clinging to life in such a body in this world? The living don't need him, but the dead would surely welcome a new friend breaking free from worldly ties.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Let's send him off.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He'll like it.
Oak Casket's words give you chills, and you finally regain your composure.
Whether someone should live or die, that's not your decision to make.
If death was indeed a form of relief, then you wouldn't know so many lingering regrets from the dead.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: That's because they didn't know the beauty of death when they were still alive.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Compared to living such a life in such a world, death is the true salvation.

options: Compared to life, death is a simpler choice.

choices.text: Compared to life, death is a simpler choice.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Perhaps you have.
But not everyone wants to be saved by death.
Just as you said, living such a life in such a world... is a much harder and painful choice than death.
But he's still chosen to live.
If a person truly wants to die, he will let you know at the necessary moment.
This is also... my response to your past.
Oak Casket stares at you for a moment, then suddenly walks over to the doctor, and pulls something out of her pocket.
Startled, you want to stop her, but then realize that Oak Casket has only pulled out a handkerchief to wipe the grime off the doctor's face.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: If you have something to say, now's the time.
But the doctor only opens his mouth and breathes laboriously.
You have no choice but to search around the small living room, trying to find some other clues. But all you can find are a few books and a notebook in the plainly furnished room.
Oak Casket just stands by the door, waiting pensively.
Before leaving, you change the doctor's nutritional fluid and clean up his bed. Suddenly, you notice that his eyes are open. He's staring intently at Oak Casket's back, his mouth moving.
You lean in and hear him mutter a word.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: ...Light.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What light?
The old doctor doesn't answer, as if uttering that word has taken all his strength. He closes his eyes again.
You catch up with Oak Casket, who seems to be avoiding something. You can barely keep up with her.
You have many questions, but at least one thing is certain: That incomprehensible regret on that stele has something to do with Oak Casket.
